steps.intent: Belgium’s objectives are to secure an immediate cessation of hostilities in Idlib, ensure unimpeded humanitarian access, protect civilians and medical infrastructure, and reinforce the UN-led political process. The main difficulties will be Russian and Chinese resistance to language demanding a halt to military operations and to accountability provisions; we expect negotiations to focus on softening those demands while retaining the humanitarian core. We will work with co-penholders Germany and Kuwait and key members to reach at least nine votes without a veto, but we will not compromise on the protection of civilians.

messages.China: China cannot support the current text as drafted: it is unbalanced, fails to address the terrorist threat in Idlib, and could create a safe haven for UN-listed terrorist groups. We need clear language in OP1 that the ceasefire does not constrain counter-terrorism operations and in OP2 that humanitarian access respects Syria's sovereignty. With those balanced amendments, China is ready to work constructively, but the current draft would not command our vote.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports the draft as it stands. We welcome its emphasis on ending hostilities, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protecting civilians, and pursuing accountability, consistent with our support for resolution 2401 and the Secretary-General’s efforts. We encourage the Council to preserve its unity and to support a text that remains humanitarian in nature and advances the political process under resolution 2254.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic supports the draft as a balanced and urgent humanitarian text. We welcome its focus on the ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and the Geneva process. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice and call on all parties to comply without delay.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the humanitarian objectives of the draft and the call for a ceasefire in Idlib. However, we cannot support a text that does not clearly preserve the fight against terrorism and the sovereignty of Syria; we therefore ask for explicit language on counter-terrorism and on humanitarian assistance in accordance with UN principles and respect for Syrian sovereignty. We also seek a clearer reaffirmation that the political process must be Syrian-led and free from external interference. We hope the penholders can accommodate these concerns to enable broad consensus.
messages.France: France supports the draft's core objectives and welcomes the focus on Idlib, humanitarian access and accountability. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 with an explicit reference to chemical weapons and cooperation with the OPCW, and OP2 with 'sustained' access and 'without undue restrictions'. We also believe OP6 should reflect the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in the political process.
messages.Germany: Germany fully supports the co-sponsored text as drafted. Our red lines are the demand for a ceasefire in OP1 and the explicit reference in OP2 to cross-border and cross-line humanitarian deliveries; these must not be weakened. We encourage the penholder to keep the text focused and resist dilution.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia supports the draft as circulated. We welcome its focus on cessation of hostilities, humanitarian access and a political solution under resolution 2254. We urge the Council to preserve its unity and call on all parties to implement the ceasefire and protect civilians.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait fully supports the current text and is proud to co-sponsor it. We ask for no changes at this stage and urge all Council members to preserve unity and adopt the resolution promptly to halt hostilities and ensure humanitarian access. Kuwait stresses implementation by all parties, respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the protection of civilians.
messages.Peru: Peru supports the draft's humanitarian focus and its call for Council unity. We ask that the reporting requirement in OP7 explicitly cover compliance with the cessation of hostilities and humanitarian access, including obstructions caused by any party. We also ask that OP5 include cooperation with relevant accountability mechanisms, consistent with Peru's position on accountability for serious violations.
messages.Poland: Poland supports the draft as an important basis for the Council to address the humanitarian crisis and ceasefire in Idlib. We ask that OP5 explicitly cover accountability for chemical weapons and resolution 2118, and that OP7 require reporting on humanitarian access and impediments. We are flexible and ready to work with the penholders to preserve Council unity.
messages.Russian Federation: We cannot support the current text, which is unbalanced and ignores the terrorist threat in Idlib. It also imposes unqualified cross-border access without the consent of the Syrian Government. We request the red-line changes above, especially an explicit counter-terrorism carve-out and removal of the cross-border language. We are prepared to work on a revised text that respects Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
messages.South Africa: South Africa supports the draft's core demands for a ceasefire and unimpeded humanitarian access. We would ask the penholder to strengthen the political horizon by reaffirming that there is no military solution and that the process must be Syrian-led and Syrian-owned, and to include an explicit call on all States to respect Syria's sovereignty and refrain from unilateral actions. With those balanced additions, South Africa is prepared to support the text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks Belgium, Germany and Kuwait for this timely and balanced draft. We fully support the text as it stands, including its demands for a ceasefire, humanitarian access through cross-border and cross-line deliveries, and accountability for violations. We urge all Council members to support it and call for its swift adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the draft resolution as presented. We strongly condemn the continued offensive in Idlib and the devastating humanitarian impact on civilians, and we call on all parties to immediately cease hostilities and allow safe, unhindered humanitarian access, including cross-border deliveries. We urge the Council to send a clear message and stand ready to vote in favour.

replies.Côte d’Ivoire: accepted: no changes requested; core humanitarian and ceasefire language retained.
replies.Dominican Republic: accepted: no changes requested; balanced humanitarian text retained.
replies.Equatorial Guinea: accepted: terrorism preambular language and new OP4 added; OP2 sovereignty/UN humanitarian principles and OP6 Syrian-led/Syrian-owned/no external interference included.
replies.France: accepted: OP2 includes sustained access and without undue restrictions; OP6 includes chemical weapons, OPCW and resolution 2118; OP7 includes women’s full, equal and meaningful participation.
replies.Germany: accepted: no changes requested; OP1 ceasefire and OP2 cross-border/cross-line references preserved.
replies.Indonesia: accepted: no changes requested; Council unity and 2254 process retained.
replies.Kuwait: accepted: no changes requested; sovereignty, implementation and humanitarian core retained.
replies.Peru: accepted: OP8 reporting now covers compliance with paragraphs 1 and 2 and access impediments by any party; OP6 includes cooperation with COI and IIIM.
replies.Poland: accepted: OP6 includes chemical weapons accountability and resolution 2118; OP8 includes humanitarian access and ceasefire compliance reporting.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: OP1 CT carve-out including HTS, OP4 terrorism/non-diversion, OP6 national prosecution language and OP8 terrorist obstacles included. OP2 keeps Council-authorized cross-border deliveries and does not condition them on Syrian Government coordination.
replies.South Africa: accepted: preambular no-military-solution/Syrian-led process added; OP1 includes CT reference; OP2 includes sovereignty; OP7 calls on Member States to respect Syria’s sovereignty and avoid destabilizing unilateral action.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: no changes requested; ceasefire, cross-border/cross-line access and accountability retained.
replies.United States of America: accepted: no changes requested; core demands on ceasefire and humanitarian access retained.

steps.summary: The revision accommodates key Chinese and Russian concerns through a terrorism carve-out with IHL safeguards, sovereignty language and reporting on terrorist obstacles, while preserving the ceasefire, cross-border/cross-line humanitarian access and accountability. It also incorporates French, Peruvian, Polish, South African and Equatorial Guinean amendments. The text is expected to secure broad support while avoiding a P5 negative vote.

messages.China: China thanks the penholder for incorporating our key concerns on counter-terrorism, sovereignty and a Syrian-led political process. We remain concerned that OP6 endorses mechanisms not established by the Security Council and could prejudge accountability issues. We request the above adjustments to keep the text balanced and consensus-oriented; with these changes, China is prepared to support the draft.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports the revised draft as a balanced humanitarian text. We welcome the retained demands for a ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability, and a Syrian-led political process under resolution 2254. We have no changes to request and encourage the Council to unite to adopt it.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic supports the revised draft as a balanced and necessary response to the deteriorating humanitarian situation in north-west Syria. We value its reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, its call for full implementation of the 30 August ceasefire, and its emphasis on unhindered humanitarian access and accountability. We also appreciate the text's clear distinctions regarding counter-terrorism operations and its support for the UN-facilitated political process under resolution 2254 (2015). We will therefore vote in favour if it is put to the vote.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea thanks the penholder for incorporating our key concerns in revision 1, particularly the counter-terrorism provisions, the reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity, the UN humanitarian principles for access, and the Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process without external interference. We therefore support the current text and have no further changes to request. We encourage all Council members to join consensus so that the Council can speak clearly on the ceasefire, humanitarian access and the political process.
messages.France: France welcomes the revised text and thanks the penholders for incorporating our priorities on sustained and unhindered humanitarian access, OPCW accountability and women’s full, equal and meaningful participation. The draft sends a necessary Council message on the ceasefire, protection of civilians and a Syrian-led political process under resolution 2254. France supports the text as it stands and calls for its prompt adoption and full implementation by all parties.
messages.Germany: Germany supports the revised draft as circulated and thanks Belgium for its inclusive penholdership. We believe the text strikes the right balance by demanding an immediate ceasefire, preserving humanitarian access, and reaffirming accountability and the political track under resolution 2254. As a co-sponsor, we urge all Council members to unite behind the text.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia supports the current draft as a balanced basis for Council action. We thank the penholder for preserving Council unity and the 2254 process, and we emphasize the importance of sovereignty, humanitarian access and protection of civilians. Indonesia will vote in favour.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the revised draft and thanks Belgium and Germany for their constructive work. As a co-sponsor, we believe the text preserves the essential balance: it demands a ceasefire in Idlib, unimpeded humanitarian access, respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and a UN-facilitated political process under resolution 2254. We urge all Council members to unite behind this text.
messages.Peru: Peru supports the current text as a balanced basis for Council action and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on reporting and accountability. We believe the Council must remain united in demanding implementation of the 30 August ceasefire, full humanitarian access, protection of civilians and a Syrian-led political process under resolution 2254 (2015). We therefore call for the text to be put to the vote without further delay and for all parties to comply with their obligations.
messages.Poland: Poland supports the revised draft as a balanced and timely response to the humanitarian and security crisis in Idlib. We welcome the incorporation of chemical-weapons accountability in OP6 and the strengthened reporting on humanitarian access and ceasefire compliance in OP8. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and call on all parties to implement the ceasefire and ensure unhindered humanitarian access without delay.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support the current text in its present form. Our red lines remain: OP2 must reflect the principle of Syrian consent and coordination with the Government of the Syrian Arab Republic, and OP6 must remove references to politicized mechanisms such as the OPCW Investigation and Identification Team and the IIIM. Without these changes, Russia will be compelled to oppose the draft.
messages.South Africa: South Africa thanks the penholder for incorporating our key concerns, including the reaffirmation that there can be no military solution, respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the call against destabilizing unilateral action. The current text is balanced and consistent with South Africa’s support for a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, unhindered humanitarian access, and combating terrorism in accordance with international law. We therefore support the draft as it stands and urge all parties to implement it in good faith.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the current draft and thanks the penholders for retaining the ceasefire, cross-border and cross-line humanitarian access, and accountability language. This text provides a balanced basis for Council action on the humanitarian crisis in Idlib and northwest Syria. We have no further changes to request and urge all members to support the draft and move to a vote without delay.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised draft. It contains the essential elements we have sought: a demand to cease hostilities in Idlib, unimpeded humanitarian access, accountability, and a clear recognition that the ceasefire does not shield ISIS, Al-Qaeda, or HTS. We urge all Council members to join consensus so the Council can speak with one voice on the need to end the violence and protect civilians.

replies.Poland: accepted: no changes requested; chemical-weapons accountability retained through OPCW FFM and resolution 2118.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: OP2 incorporates coordination with the Syrian Government and the authorized cross-border formulation; OP6 removes IIT, IIIM and COI but retains the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and chemical-weapons accountability.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: no changes requested; core ceasefire, access and accountability language retained.

steps.summary: The revised text accommodates China’s OP6 requests and Russia’s OP2 red line while narrowing accountability by removing IIT, IIIM and COI references and retaining the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and resolution 2118. It should secure broad support, with Russia likely abstaining rather than vetoing.

reasons.Belgium: Belgium is a co-penholder and co-sponsor of the draft, and it aligns with Belgium’s consistent support for humanitarian access, civilian protection, and a UN-led political process in Syria. Belgium would therefore vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.China: China joined Russia in vetoing the 19 September 2019 Idlib draft, viewing it as unbalanced and insufficiently respectful of Syrian sovereignty and counterterrorism operations; in line with its practice at this meeting, it did not take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire consistently supports humanitarian ceasefire and access resolutions on Syria and signalled support for this text in the last negotiation round. A yes vote reflects its principled support for civilian protection, sovereignty, accountability and a UN-facilitated political process.
reasons.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic supported the draft in the last negotiation round and has consistently backed ceasefire, humanitarian access, and civilian-protection measures on Syria. With no outstanding requests or changes, it would vote in favour without needing a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea had already signalled support and the draft aligns with its emphasis on humanitarian relief, sovereignty, and a UN-facilitated political process. A yes vote is consistent with its prior votes and statements on Syria.
reasons.France: The draft aligns with France’s priorities on the Idlib ceasefire, humanitarian access, accountability for chemical weapons, and the UN-led political process under resolution 2254. France therefore supports it and has no blocking concerns, helping maintain Council unity.
reasons.Germany: Germany co-sponsored the draft and consistently supports UN-led ceasefire, humanitarian access, accountability, and political settlement efforts on Syria; a yes vote with a pre-vote explanation matches that record.
reasons.Indonesia: Indonesia supported the draft in negotiations and its provisions align with Indonesia’s emphasis on humanitarian access, sovereignty, civilian protection, and a UN-facilitated Syrian-led political solution.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait is a co-sponsor and supported the draft in the final negotiation round, with no requested changes unmet. The resolution aligns with Kuwait's support for humanitarian relief, a ceasefire, Syrian sovereignty, and a UN-facilitated political process.
reasons.Peru: Peru had already indicated support and made no requests; the draft aligns with Peru's priorities on humanitarian access, protection of civilians, sovereignty, accountability and a UN-facilitated political solution. Peru therefore votes in favour and uses a pre-vote explanation to underscore those points.
reasons.Poland: Poland's established position supports humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability, and a UN-led political process in Syria; it was already recorded as supporting the draft. As an elected member, Poland would vote in favour and explain its vote before the Council.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia had opposed the draft in negotiations and its red line on chemical-weapons accountability/OPCW language was not fully accepted; the text remains unbalanced on sovereignty and counterterrorism. Moscow would therefore veto rather than allow the resolution to pass.
reasons.South Africa: South Africa supported the draft in the last negotiation round and its foreign policy favors humanitarian ceasefires, protection of civilians, and a Syrian-led political process. It would therefore vote in favour and would not need to explain its vote before the vote.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supported the draft in negotiations, with its core ceasefire, humanitarian access and accountability language consistent with UK policy on Syria. As a permanent member supportive of the text, it will vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.United States of America: The draft aligns with core US priorities on a ceasefire, humanitarian access, counterterrorism, accountability, and the UN-facilitated political process under resolution 2254. The United States indicated support, requested no changes, and would vote in favour.

before.Belgium: Belgium will vote in favour of this draft resolution, which we have submitted together with Germany and Kuwait. The humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-west Syria is alarming: civilians, medical facilities, schools and humanitarian workers continue to be attacked, and tens of thousands have been displaced. The Council cannot remain silent. We call on all parties to fully implement the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, to ensure immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, and to respect their obligations under international humanitarian law. This text is balanced. It does not shield terrorists, and it makes clear that the ceasefire does not apply to military operations against ISIL, Al-Qaeda or other designated terrorist groups, including Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, provided such operations comply with international humanitarian law. It also reaffirms Syria’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity and supports the UN-facilitated political process under resolution 2254. We urge all members to unite in support of this resolution, which responds to the needs of the Syrian people and to the Council’s responsibility to protect civilians and accountability. Belgium votes in favour.
before.Côte d’Ivoire: Mr. President, Côte d’Ivoire will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We remain gravely concerned by the humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-western Syria, including the displacement of civilians and attacks on medical and civilian infrastructure. We support the demand for the full implementation of the ceasefire and for safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria, in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We also support the text’s balanced recognition that operations against Council-designated terrorist groups must comply with international humanitarian law and human rights law. Côte d’Ivoire remains convinced that only an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under resolution 2254 can bring a lasting solution. We call on all parties to protect civilians, comply with international humanitarian law, cooperate with the OPCW and place the interests of the Syrian people above all other considerations.
before.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea votes in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because of the grave humanitarian situation in the Idlib de-escalation area and north-western Syria, and because we believe the Council must speak clearly in favour of the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, the protection of civilians, and safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need. At the same time, we reiterate the importance of respecting the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. There can be no military solution to this conflict. We call on all parties to comply with international humanitarian law, to protect civilians, medical personnel, hospitals and schools, to release all arbitrarily detained persons, and to engage seriously in the inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). Equatorial Guinea also reaffirms the need to combat terrorism in accordance with international law and the Charter of the United Nations. We urge all parties to put the interests and suffering of the Syrian people above all other considerations.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the Council’s unity in demanding the full implementation of the 30 August ceasefire in the Idlib de-escalation area and immediate, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria. The humanitarian situation, especially in north-west Syria, is unacceptable; attacks against civilians, medical personnel, hospitals and schools must stop. France reaffirms that there can be no military solution to the conflict. We support the United Nations-facilitated political process under resolution 2254 (2015), including the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, and respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We also stress the need for accountability for all violations, including the use of chemical weapons, and for full cooperation with the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons. The fight against terrorism, including Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and Al-Qaeda-linked groups, must be conducted in full compliance with international humanitarian law and human rights law.
before.Germany: Germany votes in favour of this resolution. As a co-sponsor, we believe the Security Council must speak clearly on the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-west Syria. The demand for a ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability and a genuine political process under resolution 2254 is exactly the message the Council should send. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and on all Council members to support this text.
before.Indonesia: Indonesia thanks the penholders for their efforts and will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We remain gravely concerned by the humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-western Syria, including the suffering of civilians and attacks on medical facilities, schools and other civilian infrastructure. We call on all parties to fully implement the ceasefire, ensure safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access, and comply strictly with international humanitarian law. At the same time, Indonesia reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and stresses that there can be no military solution to this conflict. Only a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations and consistent with resolution 2254 (2015), can bring lasting peace. We also underline that counter-terrorism operations must be conducted in full compliance with international humanitarian law and human rights law, and that humanitarian assistance must never be diverted to terrorist groups.
before.Kuwait: Kuwait votes in favour of this draft resolution, which we have had the honour to co-sponsor together with Belgium and Germany. We do so out of our deep concern at the deteriorating humanitarian situation in north-west Syria, including the displacement of civilians and attacks on hospitals, schools and other civilian infrastructure. We support the demand for an immediate cessation of hostilities and full implementation of the 30 August ceasefire, while preserving the right to counter terrorism in accordance with international law. We also emphasize that humanitarian access must be safe, sustained and unhindered, and must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. Kuwait reaffirms that there can be no military solution to the Syrian crisis and that the only path to lasting peace is an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. We call upon all parties to protect civilians, release arbitrarily detained persons, cooperate with the OPCW and ensure accountability for grave violations.
before.Peru: Peru thanks the penholders for their efforts and will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We remain gravely concerned by the humanitarian situation in the Idlib de-escalation area and in north-west Syria, including the displacement of civilians, civilian casualties, and attacks against medical facilities, schools and other civilian infrastructure. We call on all parties to fully implement the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, to ensure safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, and to comply strictly with international humanitarian law and human rights law. Counter-terrorism operations against ISIL, Al-Qaeda and Hayat Tahrir al-Sham must be conducted in full compliance with international law and must not become a pretext to disregard the protection of civilians. Peru reaffirms its commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and supports the United Nations-facilitated, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under resolution 2254 (2015), including the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. Accountability for all violations, including the use of chemical weapons, is essential. We believe this text sends a necessary message of Council unity in favour of protecting civilians and advancing a political solution.
before.Poland: Poland votes in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholders for their efforts to address the grave humanitarian situation in Syria, in particular in the Idlib de-escalation area. Poland has consistently supported the Security Council’s unity in demanding an end to hostilities, full implementation of the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, and immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, including through cross-line and, where authorized by the Council, cross-border deliveries. We stress the obligation of all parties to protect civilians, medical personnel, hospitals, schools and other civilian infrastructure. We also emphasize the need for accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, including the use of chemical weapons, and for full cooperation with the OPCW and full implementation of resolution 2118 (2013). Poland reaffirms that there can be no military solution to the conflict and that only an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), can bring a lasting solution. Counter-terrorism operations must be conducted in full compliance with international humanitarian law and human rights law. We call on all parties to implement this resolution without delay.
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation cannot support the draft resolution before the Council. We have consistently stated that any document on the situation in Idlib must be balanced, must respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and must not create pretexts for external interference or undermine the legitimate government’s fight against terrorism. Despite some partial adjustments, the sponsors have not taken our principal concerns into account. The text retains formulations on chemical weapons accountability that prejudge ongoing work and are used to exert pressure on Damascus, while the issues of humanitarian access and sovereignty are addressed in a one-sided manner. The draft also fails to reflect the realities on the ground and the efforts of the Syrian Government and its partners in combating terrorist groups, including those linked to Al-Qaeda. For these reasons, the Russian delegation will vote against the draft.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom supports this draft resolution and will vote in favour. The humanitarian situation in north-west Syria remains appalling, and the ceasefire of 30 August must be implemented in full by all parties. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian regime and its backers, to allow safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, including through cross-border deliveries where authorised, and to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure. Accountability for all violations, including the use of chemical weapons, is essential. The United Kingdom remains committed to a Syrian-led, Syrian-owned political process under resolution 2254. Council unity on these issues is important, and we urge all members to support the resolution.
before.United States of America: The United States supports this resolution and thanks Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait for their work. The ceasefire in Idlib must be implemented immediately, and all parties must allow safe, sustained, and unhindered humanitarian access to those in need. We welcome the resolution’s clear recognition that the ceasefire does not apply to military operations against ISIL and Al-Qaeda-linked terrorist groups, including Hayat Tahrir al-Sham. The United States also stresses the need for accountability, including for chemical weapons use, and reaffirms that there can be no lasting solution without a genuine Syrian-led political process under resolution 2254. We call on the Assad regime and its backers to end attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure and to comply fully with their international obligations.

after.Belgium: Mr President, Belgium regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait. Thirteen members voted in favour. The negative votes of two permanent members have prevented the Council from speaking with one voice at a moment when civilians in Idlib and north-west Syria urgently need it. We thank all delegations that supported the text. Its objectives remain fully valid: full implementation of the ceasefire of 30 August 2019; immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need; protection of civilians, medical personnel, hospitals, schools and other civilian infrastructure; accountability for violations; and a genuine Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under resolution 2254 (2015), in full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria. The Council’s inability to adopt this text does not relieve any party of its obligations under international humanitarian law and human rights law. Belgium will continue to work for Council unity and for the protection of civilians in Syria.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted against the draft resolution just now. China is gravely concerned about the humanitarian situation in Syria, including in Idlib and north-western Syria. We support an immediate ceasefire, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the provision of humanitarian assistance to all those in need. At the same time, humanitarian access must respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and must be implemented in coordination with the Syrian Government.

China believes the draft before the Council was not balanced. It did not fully take into account the legitimate concerns of relevant parties, particularly on humanitarian access, chemical weapons accountability and counter-terrorism. The language on chemical weapons could prejudge the work of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons and be used to exert pressure on Syria. The text also risked creating pretexts for external interference in Syria’s internal affairs. China has consistently held that there can be no military solution to the Syrian issue. The only way out is an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations and in accordance with resolution 2254, without external interference.

China’s negative vote does not mean indifference to the humanitarian suffering of the Syrian people. It is a responsible step aimed at upholding the authority and unity of the Security Council and avoiding the adoption of a one-sided and divisive text. China remains ready to work with all Council members to find a balanced solution that is conducive to a ceasefire, to humanitarian relief, to counter-terrorism and to a political settlement of the Syrian issue.
after.Côte d’Ivoire:
Mr. President,

Côte d’Ivoire takes the floor to express its deep regret that the draft resolution submitted by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait was not adopted, notwithstanding the broad support it received in the Council. We thank the sponsors for their efforts to mobilise the Council in the face of the alarming humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-western Syria, where civilians, medical personnel, hospitals and schools continue to bear the brunt of the conflict.

Our vote in favour reflected our conviction that the Council must speak clearly in support of the full implementation of the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, and the protection of civilians in accordance with international humanitarian law. Those imperatives have not disappeared with the failure of this draft.

Côte d’Ivoire reiterates its respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We remain convinced that there can be no military solution to the conflict and that only an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations and consistent with resolution 2254 (2015), can bring a lasting peace to Syria. We call upon all Council members to preserve the unity of this body and to continue to engage constructively so that the Council can discharge its responsibilities and help alleviate the suffering of the Syrian people.
after.Dominican Republic:
Mr. President,

The Dominican Republic voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait. We wish to explain our position. We remain gravely concerned by the humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-western Syria, including the displacement of civilians, civilian casualties and attacks against hospitals, schools and other civilian infrastructure. We supported this text because it called for the full implementation of the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, the protection of civilians and medical personnel, the release of arbitrarily detained persons, accountability for serious violations, and a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under resolution 2254 (2015), including the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. The text also reaffirmed the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

We regret that the Council was unable to adopt this resolution. The humanitarian imperative in Syria must not become a casualty of political division. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and civilian objects, fully implement the ceasefire and facilitate humanitarian access. The Dominican Republic will continue to support the unity of the Security Council and a peaceful political solution to the Syrian conflict.
after.Equatorial Guinea:
Mr President,

Equatorial Guinea voted in favour of this draft resolution because we could not remain indifferent to the humanitarian tragedy in Idlib and north-western Syria. We deeply regret that the Security Council has not been able to adopt a text supported by thirteen members and aimed at reinforcing the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, protecting civilians and ensuring safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access. This outcome should not discourage us. The humanitarian emergency is real, and the civilian population cannot be held hostage to political differences.

We take note of the concerns raised by the members that voted against the draft. We believe that those concerns can and must be addressed through dialogue and constructive consultations, not by leaving the Council silent. Equatorial Guinea therefore calls on all members to continue negotiations in a spirit of compromise so that the Council can speak with one voice on a balanced text that respects the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and the principle of non-interference.

We reiterate that there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria. We call on all parties to implement the ceasefire, to protect civilians, medical personnel, hospitals, schools and other civilian infrastructure, to allow humanitarian access to all those in need, and to engage seriously in the inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations under resolution 2254 (2015). Equatorial Guinea remains ready to work with all Council members to that end.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of this draft resolution and deeply regrets that it was not adopted owing to the negative votes of two permanent members. The Council has just failed to respond to a humanitarian emergency and to support the implementation of the ceasefire of 30 August. That is a serious and regrettable outcome, because the text was balanced: it demanded an end to hostilities, full respect for international humanitarian law and unhindered humanitarian access, while preserving operations against terrorist groups designated by the Council and reaffirming Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

France recalls that the humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-west Syria remains unacceptable. Attacks against civilians, medical personnel, hospitals and schools must stop. The 30 August ceasefire must be fully implemented by all parties without delay. Humanitarian access — cross-line and, where authorized by the Council, cross-border — must be safe, sustained and unhindered. These obligations derive from international humanitarian law and are not subject to political conditions.

The absence of a Council decision does not relieve any party of its responsibilities. France calls on all parties, in particular the Syrian regime and its backers, to respect international humanitarian law and to protect civilians. Accountability for all violations remains essential, including for the use of chemical weapons. The work of the OPCW and the full implementation of resolution 2118 (2013) must continue.

There can be no military solution in Syria. France remains committed to a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under resolution 2254 (2015), with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. France will continue to work with all Council members to defend the humanitarian imperative and the credibility of this Council. We cannot allow the veto to become a licence to ignore the suffering of the Syrian people.

Thank you.
after.Germany:
Germany voted in favour of this resolution and was proud to co-sponsor it together with Belgium and Kuwait. We deeply regret that the Council has not been able to adopt this balanced and urgently needed text. The humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-west Syria remains catastrophic. Civilians, medical personnel, hospitals, schools and humanitarian workers must be protected. The ceasefire of 30 August must be implemented by all parties, and safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access must be ensured for all those in need.

The failure of this Council to speak with one voice today does not change the facts on the ground, nor does it diminish our responsibility. Germany will continue to work with all Council members to support the implementation of resolution 2254, a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process, accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, and full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We call on all parties and all Council members to remain engaged and to act in the interests of the Syrian people.
after.Kuwait:
Mr. President,

Kuwait voted in favour of the draft resolution, which we co-sponsored, and we regret that the Council has not been able to adopt it. We had hoped that the Council would speak with one voice in response to the grave humanitarian situation in north-western Syria, including the displacement of civilians and attacks against hospitals, schools and other civilian infrastructure.

The failure to adopt this resolution does not diminish the obligations of the parties. Kuwait calls on all parties to fully implement the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, to ensure safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need, and to comply strictly with international humanitarian law. Operations against terrorist groups must be conducted in full conformity with international law and must not be used as a pretext to disregard the protection of civilians.

Kuwait reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and stresses that there can be no military solution to the crisis. Only an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process, facilitated by the United Nations and consistent with resolution 2254 (2015), can bring a lasting solution. We also call for the release of all arbitrarily detained persons and for accountability for all violations.

Kuwait will continue to support humanitarian efforts and the work of the Secretary-General and his Special Envoy. We urge the Council to preserve its unity and remain actively engaged on this issue, which is of grave importance to the Syrian people and to the region.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has voted against the draft resolution before the Council, and we wish to explain that vote. Our position was set out before the vote, but we consider it necessary to state once again that the text was not balanced and did not reflect the real situation in Idlib and north-western Syria. We regret that the sponsors were not prepared to take into account the principal concerns of the Russian Federation. A resolution on such a sensitive matter cannot be built on one-sided assessments and cannot ignore the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

The draft placed the main emphasis on demands addressed to the Syrian Government and its allies, while failing to give an objective picture of the terrorist threat. The security situation in Idlib is determined above all by the presence of Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and other Al-Qaeda-linked groups. The provisions of the text on a ceasefire, however carefully worded, could in practice create conditions for terrorists to regroup and rearm. Russia has consistently supported a ceasefire, including the understandings of 30 August 2019, and the implementation of the Sochi memorandum. But a ceasefire must not become a cover for terrorism. The fight against Council-designated terrorist groups must continue, and any operations must of course be conducted in compliance with international humanitarian law.

We are also seriously concerned by attempts to impose humanitarian mechanisms that bypass the legitimate Government of Syria. Humanitarian assistance must reach those in need, including through cross-line deliveries and, where authorized by the Security Council, cross-border deliveries. But such assistance must respect Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, be carried out in coordination with the Syrian Government, and not be used as a tool of political pressure or to support illegal armed groups. Russia is not indifferent to the suffering of Syrian civilians. We have repeatedly called for unhindered humanitarian access and for the protection of civilians, medical personnel and civilian infrastructure.

We rejected the draft also because of the unacceptable approach to the chemical dossier. Responsibility for the use of chemical weapons must be established on the basis of reliable, objective and professionally verified facts, within the framework of the Chemical Weapons Convention and in cooperation with the OPCW. The Russian Federation opposes attempts to prejudge the outcome of investigations and to use the chemical file for pressure on Damascus.

The Russian Federation remains committed to a political settlement in Syria based on resolution 2254 (2015), a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned process without external interference, and the full implementation of the decisions agreed by the Syrians themselves, including the work of the Constitutional Committee. We will continue to cooperate constructively with all Council members on balanced documents that genuinely help the Syrian people, respect Syria’s sovereignty and do not undermine the fight against terrorism. Our negative vote today was a vote against a flawed and one-sided draft, not against humanitarian assistance or a political settlement.
after.South Africa:
Mr. President,

South Africa voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. We did so because of our grave concern at the humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-western Syria, including the displacement of civilians and attacks against medical personnel, hospitals, schools and other civilian infrastructure. The protection of civilians and safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need must remain the Council’s immediate priority. South Africa regrets that the draft was not adopted, despite the support of the overwhelming majority of Council members. Humanitarian need in Syria does not disappear because the Council is divided.

South Africa reiterates that all parties must comply with international humanitarian law and human rights law, fully implement the ceasefire of 30 August 2019, and ensure humanitarian access in accordance with the guiding principles of humanitarian assistance and in full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We stress that counter-terrorism operations must be conducted in full conformity with international law and must not be used as a pretext to disregard the protection of civilians. Humanitarian assistance must not be diverted to terrorist groups.

There can be no military solution to the Syrian conflict. South Africa reaffirms the centrality of a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned inclusive political process, facilitated by the United Nations and in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). We call upon all external actors to respect Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and to refrain from unilateral actions that could further inflame tensions. We also support the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in the political process, the release of all arbitrarily detained persons and accountability for serious violations, including the use of chemical weapons.

The Security Council must speak with one voice on the protection of civilians and on the political settlement of the Syrian crisis. South Africa will continue to support United Nations-led mediation efforts and urges the Council to remain actively engaged, in a balanced and constructive manner, in the search for a peaceful solution that safeguards Syria’s sovereignty and serves the legitimate aspirations of the Syrian people.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution and deeply regrets that it has not been adopted. The humanitarian situation in Idlib and north-west Syria remains dire: civilians are being killed, hospitals and schools are being attacked, and humanitarian access is being obstructed. The Council had before it a balanced text that demanded full implementation of the 30 August ceasefire, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and accountability for violations, including the use of chemical weapons. It is deeply disappointing that the vetoes of the Russian Federation and China have prevented the Council from speaking with one voice on these vital issues. The United Kingdom will continue to support the United Nations, the Special Envoy and all efforts to achieve a Syrian-led, Syrian-owned political settlement under resolution 2254. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian regime and its backers, to end attacks on civilians and to allow immediate, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President, the United States takes the floor to express our deep disappointment at the outcome of this vote. Thirteen members of this Council supported a balanced and urgent text demanding implementation of the 30 August ceasefire, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and medical facilities, and accountability for violations. The resolution also made clear that the ceasefire does not shield ISIL, Al-Qaeda or Hayat Tahrir al-Sham from military operations conducted in compliance with international humanitarian law. We thank Belgium, Germany and Kuwait for their leadership.

The vetoes cast today do not diminish the obligations of all parties — above all the Assad regime and its backers — to comply with international humanitarian law, end attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, and allow humanitarian access to all those in need. The United States will continue to support the Syrian people, press for a genuine Syrian-led political process under resolution 2254, and insist on accountability for all violations, including the use of chemical weapons. This Council's failure today must not become a license for further suffering.
